titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Lot's Daughters: Moab and Ammon (ch. 78–79)
part: ch. 78–79 — Lot's Daughters: Moab and Ammon
about: The author shows that the kings of Moab and Amalek are of Shem's seed by retelling Genesis 19: God sends the angels Michael and Gabriel to bring Lot out of Sodom, his wife turns to a pillar of salt, and his two daughters make him drunk in turn; the elder bears Moab, the younger Ammon, said here to be the king of the Amalekites.

sentences.t: ፸፰ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሞአብ ።
sentences.l: 78. Concerning king-of Moab.
sentences.i: Chapter 78: Concerning the King of Moab
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፸፰ is the Ethiopic numeral 70 + 8 = 78. በእንተ 'concerning' governs ንጉሠ ሞአብ 'king-of Moab', a construct chain: the first noun takes the construct shape ንጉሠ and is read 'of' the next.

sentences.t: ወንጉሠ ፡ ሞአብሂ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ወናየድዐክሙ ፡ ዘከመሂ ፡ ኮነ ።
sentences.l: And-king-of Moab-also seed-of Shem he, and-we-will-inform-you how-also it-was.
sentences.i: Now the king of Moab too is of the seed of Shem, and we shall tell you how that came about.
sentences.n: ወ- 'and' opens the unit; the enclitic -ሂ on ሞአብሂ is 'also, too', continuing the series of kings shown to be of Shem. ወንጉሠ ሞአብ and ዘርአ ሴም are construct chains ('king-of Moab', 'seed-of Shem'); ውእቱ 'he' is the copula 'is'. ወናየድዐክሙ is ወ- + ናየድዐክሙ 'we shall inform you', the ʾa-stem (causative) of the root ydʿ with the object -ክሙ 'you (pl.)', as in ch. 77. ዘከመሂ is ዘ + ከመ 'how' + -ሂ; ኮነ 'it was, it came about'. This unit opens the Moab story, which is told from Genesis 19.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ አፍለሶ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ እምሀገረ ፡ አቡሁ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ካራን ፡ ወለሎጥኒ ፡ አዕደዎ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ውስተ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ሰዶም ፡ ወገሞራ ፤
sentences.l: And-when he-removed-him God to-Abraham from-city-of his-father into land-of Haran, and-Lot-also he-caused-to-cross-him God into land-of Sodom and-Gomorrah;
sentences.i: When God moved Abraham from the city of his father to the land of Haran, he also brought Lot across into the land of Sodom and Gomorrah;
sentences.n: ወሶበ is ወ- 'and' + ሶበ 'when'. አፍለሶ 'he removed him' is the causative (ʾa-stem) of ፈለሰ 'migrate', with -ሶ 'him'; ለአብርሃም has ለ- marking the object ('Abraham'), the object being named after the verb that already carries -ሶ. እምሀገረ አቡሁ: እም- 'from' + the construct ሀገረ 'city-of' + አቡሁ 'his father'; ምድረ ካራን is 'land-of Haran'. ወለሎጥኒ is ወ- + ለ- (object marker) + ሎጥ + enclitic -ኒ 'also'. አዕደዎ is the causative of ዐደወ 'cross over' (I take the root so, not confirmed in Dillmann (?)) with -ዎ 'him'. ሰዶም ወገሞራ are Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19); the unit ends at ፤ and the clause continues.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ያጥፍኦሙ ፡ ለሰብአ ፡ ሰዶም ፡ ወገሞራ ፡ ፈነወ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ መላእክቲሁ ፡ ሚካኤል ፡ ወገብርኤል ፡ ከመ ፡ ያውፅእዎ ፡ ለሎጥ ፡ ወያውዕይዋ ፡ ለሀገረ ፡ ሰዶም ፡ ወገሞራ ፤
sentences.l: And-when he-wished God that he-destroy-them to-men-of Sodom and-Gomorrah, he-sent God his-angels, Michael and-Gabriel, that they-bring-out-him to-Lot and-they-burn-her to-city-of Sodom and-Gomorrah;
sentences.i: and when God wished to destroy the men of Sodom and Gomorrah, God sent his angels Michael and Gabriel to bring Lot out and to burn the city of Sodom and Gomorrah;
sentences.n: ከመ ያጥፍኦሙ 'that he destroy them' is ከመ + a subjunctive of the causative (ʾa-stem) of ጠፍአ 'perish', with -ሙ 'them'; ለሰብአ ሰዶም has ለ- marking the object and the construct ሰብአ 'men-of'. መላእክቲሁ 'his angels' is the plural of መልአክ + -ሁ; Michael and Gabriel are named as the angels sent; Genesis 19:1 speaks only of 'two angels'. ከመ ያውፅእዎ ለሎጥ 'that they bring him out, Lot' is the causative of ወፅአ 'go out', again with ለ- marking the doubled object. ወያውዕይዋ ለሀገረ is 'and they burn her, the city' (the causative of ወዐየ 'burn' as I read it (?)); the city is feminine, hence -ዋ 'her'.

sentences.t: ወአማሰኑ ፡ ኪያሃ ፡ ወአውፅእዎ ፡ ለሎጥ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ደቂቁ ፡ ወብእሲቱሰ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ተመይጠት ፡ ድኅሬሃ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትርአይ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ አቡሃ ፡ ወእማ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-destroyed her, and-they-brought-out to-Lot with his-children; and-his-wife-as-for when she-turned behind-her that she-see city-of her-father and-her-mother;
sentences.i: and they destroyed the city, and brought Lot out with his children; but his wife, when she turned back, wishing to see the city of her father and her mother —
sentences.n: ወአማሰኑ ኪያሃ 'and they destroyed her' is the causative of ማሰነ 'perish' with the independent object ኪያሃ 'her' (the city, feminine). ወአውፅእዎ is ወ- + 'they brought him out', Lot named after it with ለ- marking the object (as in the last unit). ደቂቁ 'his children' is ደቂቅ + -ሁ. In ወብእሲቱሰ the -ሰ is a contrastive 'as for' (as in ወውእቱሰ): 'but his wife'. ተመይጠት 'she turned' is the 3fs perfect of the tä-stem of the root m-y-ṭ; ድኅሬሃ 'behind her' means 'back'. ከመ ትርአይ is the subjunctive 'that she see'; ሀገረ አቡሃ ወእማ 'the city of her father and her mother' (hers: -ሃ). The sentence about the wife is left hanging and is taken up in the unit beginning ወሶበ ሰምዐት. The allusion is Genesis 19:26, Lot's wife.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ወረደ ፡ መዐተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ላዕለ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ሰዶም ፡ ዝናመ ፡ እሳት ፡ እምሰማይ ፡ ዘያነድድ ፡ አድባረ ፡ ወአውግረ ፡ አእባነ ፡ ወመሬተ ፡ ወይወርድ ፡ መባርቅት ፡ ወፀዓዓት ፡ ወነጐድጓድ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ድምፀ ፡ መዐተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወደመና ፡ እሳትኒ ፡ ዘያጠይሶ ፡ ለመርቄ ፤
sentences.l: For he-came-down wrath-of God upon city-of Sodom, rain-of fire from-heaven that-burns mountains and-hills (?) stones and-earth, and-descend lightnings and-(?) and-thunder with voice-of wrath-of God, and-cloud fire-also that-blackens (?) to-(?);
sentences.i: For the wrath of God came down upon the city of Sodom, a rain of fire from heaven that burns mountains and hills, stones and earth, and lightnings and (?) and thunder come down with the voice of God's wrath, and a cloud of fire as well that blackens (?) the (?);
sentences.n: እስመ 'for'. ወረደ 'it came down' (the ወ is part of the root w-r-d); the subject መዐተ እግዚኣብሔር 'wrath-of God' is a construct chain and ዝናመ እሳት 'rain-of fire' is in apposition to it. Genesis 19:24 describes the rain of sulfur and fire. ዘያነድድ 'that burns' is ዘ + the imperfect of the ʾa-stem of ነደደ 'burn'. አድባረ is the plural 'mountains' (of ደብር), read here as an accusative in a list (it could instead be a construct, 'mountains and hills of stones and earth' (?)); ወአውግረ አእባነ ወመሬተ 'and hills (?), stones and earth': አውግር I take as a plural 'hills' but could not confirm it (?). ወይወርድ 'and he/it descends' is ወ- + imperfect. መባርቅት 'lightnings' and ነጐድጓድ 'thunder' are clear; ወፀዓዓት is not a word I could place, perhaps another meteor such as hail or thunderclaps (?). ድምፀ መዐተ is a double construct, 'voice-of wrath-of'. In ወደመና እሳትኒ the -ኒ is 'also'. ዘያጠይሶ ለመርቄ: ያጠይሶ I take as the ʾa-stem of a verb 'blacken' (?), and መርቄ I cannot identify (a place or a thing; ለ- marks it as object) (?); so the end of this unit is uncertain.

sentences.t: ወዝንቱ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ተሰምዐ ፡ ድምፅ ፡ ይቤልዎ ፡ መላእክት ፡ ለሎጥ ፡ ኢትትመየጡ ፡ ድኅረ ፡ እምከመ ፡ ወፃእክሙ ፡ እምሀገርክሙ ፡ ኢትትመየጡ ፡ ድኅሬክሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ሞተ ፡ ኢትሙቱ ፤
sentences.l: And-this all when it-was-heard the-sound, they-said-to-him angels to-Lot: not-turn-back after since you-went-out from-your-city not-turn-back behind-you, that death not-you-die;
sentences.i: And when all this, the sound, was heard, the angels said to Lot: 'Do not turn back; after you have gone out of your city do not turn back behind you, that you may not die.'
sentences.n: ወዝንቱ ኵሉ 'and all this', the topic placed before the clause; ሶበ ተሰምዐ ድምፅ 'when the sound was heard', ተሰምዐ the passive (tä-stem) of ሰምዐ 'hear'. ይቤልዎ 'they said to him' is ይቤሉ + ሎ ('to him'), with ለሎጥ restating who is meant. ኢትትመየጡ is the negative jussive (2mp) of the tä-stem of m-y-ṭ, a warning not to turn back; the plural addresses Lot with his household (Genesis 19:17 has the singular, so the plural is this text's own). ድኅረ እምከመ ወፃእክሙ: ድኅረ 'after', እምከመ 'since, when', ወፃእክሙ 'you (pl.) went out' (ወፅአ). ከመ ሞተ ኢትሙቱ is literally 'that you not die the death' (ሞተ here as a noun 'death' with a figura etymologica: ሞተ ... ኢትሙቱ), which I render 'that you may not die'; the form ሞተ can also be read as the verb 'he died', so the clause is a little uncertain (?).

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ሰምዐት ፡ ይእቲ ፡ ብእሲተ ፡ ሎጥ ፡ አቅማባ ፡ ተመይጠት ፡ ድኅሬሃ ፡ ወኮነት ፡ ሐውልተ ፡ ፄው ፡ ወሀለወት ፡ እስከ ፡ ዮም ፡ ወእስከ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ ዕለት ፡ ወለሎጥሰ ፡ እኁሁ ፡ ለአብርሃም ፡ አንበሮ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ውስተ ፡ አድባረ ፡ አራራት ፨
sentences.l: And-when she-heard she, wife-of Lot, Aqmaba (?), she-turned behind-her, and-she-became pillar-of salt, and-she-is until today and-until this day; and-to-Lot-as-for his-brother to-Abraham he-settled-him God in mountains-of Ararat;
sentences.i: And when she heard — the wife of Lot, Aqmaba (?) — she turned back and became a pillar of salt, and she is there to this day, to this very day. But Lot, the brother of Abraham, God settled in the mountains of Ararat.
sentences.n: ወሶበ ሰምዐት ይእቲ ብእሲተ ሎጥ: ሰምዐት is 'she heard' (3fs), ይእቲ 'she' repeats the subject, and ብእሲተ ሎጥ is a construct chain 'wife-of Lot'. አቅማባ follows with no marker; I take it as the wife's name, since Bezold gives no other sense (?). She is the woman of Genesis 19:26, turned to ሐውልተ ፄው 'pillar-of salt' (ሐውልት is accusative; ፄው 'salt'). ወሀለወት 'she is there, exists' (ሀሎ); እስከ ዮም ወእስከ ዛቲ ዕለት 'until today and until this day'. ወለሎጥሰ: ለ- marks the object, -ሰ is 'as for'. እኁሁ ለአብርሃም 'his brother, Abraham's' is the text's wording; Genesis calls Lot Abraham's nephew, and 'brother' fits the loose sense of Genesis 14:14. አንበሮ is 'he settled him' (ነበረ causative). The mountains of Ararat (አራራት, Genesis 8:4) is the text's place; Genesis puts Lot in the hills near Zoar. The ፨ ends the account of Lot's rescue and opens the next scene.

sentences.t: ወተከለ ፡ ወይነ ፡ ሐዲሰ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-planted vine new;
sentences.i: And he planted a new vine;
sentences.n: ተከለ 'he planted' (3ms perfect, subject Lot); ወይነ is the accusative of ወይን, which means both 'wine' and 'vine'. After a verb of planting I take 'vine', with ሐዲሰ 'new' as its adjective (accusative); the other sense, 'wine', is possible (?). The planting of a vineyard is the story of Noah, Genesis 9:20, which the text compares in the unit beginning ወኖኅሂ.

sentences.t: ወአስተያሁ ፡ ወይነ ፡ ለአቡሆን ፡ አዋልዲሁ ፡ እስመ ፡ መከራ ፡ ምክረ ፡ እኪተ ፡ ወይቤላ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ንዋየ ፡ አቡነ ፡ በአይቴ ፡ ይጠፍእ ፤
sentences.l: And-they-made-drink-him wine to-their-father, his-daughters, for they-took-counsel counsel evil, and-he-said-to-her (?): this goods-of our-father, in-where does-it-perish;
sentences.i: His daughters made their father drink wine, for they planned an evil plan, and one said to the other: 'This estate of our father — how is it to be lost?
sentences.n: ወአስተያሁ 'and they (fem.) made him drink': the ʾa-stem of ሰትየ 'drink', in the 3fp perfect (አስተያ) with -ሁ 'him'; subject አዋልዲሁ 'his daughters' follows, and ለአቡሆን 'to their father' (-ሆን is 'their (fem.)'). For the story see Genesis 19:30-38. እስመ መከራ ምክረ እኪተ: መከራ I take as the 3fp perfect (-ā, as in the ወአስተያሁ just before, with አዋልዲሁ 'his daughters' as the subject) of መከረ 'take counsel, plan', 'they (both) took counsel', with ምክረ እኪተ 'an evil counsel' as its cognate object. ይቤላ 'he said to her' is masculine and singular in form where a feminine speaker (ትቤላ, as in ch. 79) is expected; I read it as one daughter speaking to the other, with the masculine form standing for ትቤላ, so the clause is uncertain (?). The speech: ንዋየ አቡነ is a construct chain 'goods-of our-father', and the word may mean his property or his line; በአይቴ ይጠፍእ 'in what way will it perish?' (I take the sense 'how', not confirmed in Dillmann (?)). The speech runs into the next unit.

sentences.t: እምነኬ ፡ ተሀጒለት ፡ በፍኖት ፡ ወለነኒ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ዘያወስበነ ፡ በዝየ ።
sentences.l: Our-mother-indeed she-perished on-road, and-for-us-also none who-will-marry-us here.
sentences.i: Our mother has perished on the road, and for us too there is no one to marry us here.'
sentences.n: እምነኬ is እምነ 'our mother' + the emphatic -ኬ 'indeed'. ተሀጒለት 'she perished' is the tä-stem of ሀጐለ 'be lost' in the 3fs. በፍኖት 'on the road'. ወለነኒ is ወ- + ለ- + -ነ 'us' + -ኒ 'also'. አልቦ 'there is none' (negative existential) is followed by the relative ዘያወስበነ 'who will marry us': the ʾa-stem of ወሰበ 'take a wife', which I read as 'give a husband to, marry us', not confirmed in Dillmann (?). በዝየ 'here'. The daughters' reasoning is that of Genesis 19:31, where the elder says there is no man left in the land.

sentences.t: ወአስከራሁ ፡ ለአቡሆን ፡ ወሰከበት ፡ እንተ ፡ ትልህቅ ፡ ወለቱ ፡ ምስሌሁ ፡ ኅበ ፡ ጸልመ ፡ ልቡ ፡ በወይን ፤
sentences.l: And-they-made-drunk-him to-their-father, and-she-lay she who is-elder his-daughter with-him, where it-was-darkened his-heart with-wine;
sentences.i: So they made their father drunk, and the elder, his daughter, lay with him, at a time when his mind was clouded with wine;
sentences.n: ወአስከራሁ 'and they (the two) made him drunk' is the 3fp perfect (-ā, as in ወአስተያሁ) of the ʾa-stem of ሰከረ 'be drunk', with -ሁ 'him'; the verb then turns to the elder alone (ሰከበት). ሰከበት 'she lay down' (3fs perfect); እንተ ትልህቅ 'she who is elder' (the relative with the imperfect of ልህቀ 'grow great'; the same phrase is in ch. 79), with ወለቱ 'his daughter' added in apposition. ኅበ is a spelling of ኀበ 'where, when', here a conjunction; ጸልመ ልቡ 'his heart was darkened', ልብ also means 'mind'. This is Genesis 19:33.

sentences.t: ወሎጥሰ ፡ ጻድቅ ፡ ኢያእመረ ፡ በሰኪቦታ ፡ ለወለቱ ፡ ወኢያእመረ ፡ በተንሥኦታ ፡ ለወለቱ ፡ እስመ ፡ ስካር ፡ ያጸልም ፡ ልቦ ።
sentences.l: And-Lot-as-for righteous not-he-knew in-her-lying-down of-his-daughter and-not-he-knew in-her-rising of-his-daughter, for drunkenness it-darkens his-heart.
sentences.i: Now Lot, a righteous man, did not know when his daughter lay down, nor when she rose, for drunkenness darkens the mind.
sentences.n: ወሎጥሰ 'and Lot, as for him' (the -ሰ is contrastive). ጻድቅ 'righteous' is a descriptive adjective set beside the name. ኢያእመረ 'he did not know' (negative of the ʾa-stem አእመረ 'know'; ወኢያእመረ repeats it); በሰኪቦታ and በተንሥኦታ are በ- 'at' + a verbal noun + -ታ '3fs her' ('her lying down', 'her rising'), each with ለወለቱ 'of his daughter' naming whose. The wording is that of Genesis 19:33, 'he did not know when she lay down or when she rose'. እስመ ስካር ያጸልም ልቦ 'for drunkenness darkens his heart (mind)': ያጸልም is the ʾa-stem imperfect of ጸልመ, picking up the verb of the last unit. The exact form of the verbal nouns (ሰኪቦት, from ሰከበ) I could not check (?).

sentences.t: ወኖኅሂ ፡ በስካር ፡ ኮነ ፡ ዕሩቀ ፡ እምብእሲቱ ፡ ወደቂቁ ፡ እስከ ፡ ይረግም ፡ ውሉዶ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ሰሐቆ ፤
sentences.l: And-Noah-also in-drunkenness he-became naked from-his-wife and-his-children, until he-curse his-son to-him-who he-mocked-him;
sentences.i: Noah too, in drunkenness, became naked before his wife and his sons, until he cursed his son, the one who had mocked him;
sentences.n: ወኖኅሂ is ወ- + ኖኅ 'Noah' + -ሂ 'also': the text offers Noah as a second example of wine taking away judgement (Genesis 9:20-27, the curse after Ham's mockery). ኮነ ዕሩቀ 'he became naked' (ዕሩቀ is the accusative predicate); እምብእሲቱ ወደቂቁ 'from his wife and his children' I take as 'before, in the sight of' them, though the Geʿez is literally 'from' (?). እስከ ይረግም 'until he cursed' (እስከ with the imperfect). ውሉዶ ለዘ ሰሐቆ: ውሉዶ 'his son' (ውሉድ + -ሁ) is the object, restated by ለዘ ሰሐቆ 'to him who mocked him'; ሰሐቀ is 'laugh, mock'. The curse in Genesis falls on Canaan, Ham's son; the text says only 'his son' and I leave it so.

sentences.t: ወለሎጥሰ ፡ ኢተኆለቆ ፡ ኀጢአተ ፡ እስመ ፡ በኢያእምሮ ፡ ገብረ ።
sentences.l: And-to-Lot-as-for not-it-was-counted-to-him sin (?), for in-not-knowledge he-did.
sentences.i: But for Lot sin was not counted, for he acted without knowing.
sentences.n: ወለሎጥሰ 'but as for Lot'; ኢተኆለቆ 'it was not counted to him' is the negated tä-stem of ኆለቈ 'count' (the house lemma), the final -ቆ read as ቀ + -ሁ 'to him' (it may instead be a spelling of ተኆለቈ (?)), so 'sin was not reckoned (to him)', ኀጢአተ being an accusative that remains with the passive; ለሎጥ marks the one to whom it was not counted. እስመ 'for'; በኢያእምሮ 'in not-knowing' is በ- + the negative ኢ- + a verbal noun; ገብረ 'he did' (3ms perfect of ገብረ). The text is excusing Lot, which Genesis does not do in so many words, though Genesis 19:33 says he did not know.

sentences.t: ወፀንሰት ፡ ወወለደት ፡ እንተ ፡ ትልህቅ ፡ ወሰመየቶ ፡ ስሞ ፡ ሞአብ ፡ እምኀበ ፡ አቡየ ፡ በብርክየ ፡ ብሂል ፤
sentences.l: And-she-conceived and-she-bore she who is-elder, and-she-named-him his-name Moab, from my-father, in-my-knee (?), meaning;
sentences.i: The elder conceived and bore a son and named him Moab, which means 'from my father, in my lap' (?);
sentences.n: ወፀንሰት ወወለደት 'she conceived and bore' (3fs perfects). እንተ ትልህቅ 'the elder' (as above). ወሰመየቶ ስሞ ሞአብ: ሰመየ 'name' with -ቶ 'him', and ስሞ 'his name' stands in apposition, 'she named him, his name Moab'. The etymology: እምኀበ አቡየ 'from (beside) my father', plain; በብርክየ is በ- + ብርክ 'knee, lap' + -የ 'my', and I am not sure that this is the word or its sense here (?). ብሂል is 'saying, meaning', a noun marking an explanation. Genesis 19:37 names the child Moab; the explanation 'from the father' is a Hebrew-style etymology, and the second phrase is this text's addition.

sentences.t: ወውእቱኬ ፡ አቡሆሙ ፡ ለሞአባውያን ፡ ወለአጋራዊያን ።
sentences.l: And-he-indeed father-of-them to-Moabites and-to-Hagarites.
sentences.i: He is the father of the Moabites and of the Hagarites (?).
sentences.n: ወውእቱኬ 'and he indeed' (-ኬ emphatic); አቡሆሙ 'their father', then ለሞአባውያን 'to the Moabites', the ለ- naming the possessors (so 'the father of them, of the Moabites'). ወለአጋራዊያን is the same with ወ- 'and'; አጋራዊያን I read as 'Hagarites' (people of Hagar) from the name አጋር, but I could not confirm it (?). Genesis 19:37 gives Moab only as father of the Moabites.

sentences.t: ናሁኬ ፡ ተዐውቀ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ሞአብሂ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሴም ፡ ውእቱ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: Behold-indeed it-became-known king-of Moab-also that seed-of Shem he. ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: So now it is known that the king of Moab too is of the seed of Shem.
sentences.n: ናሁኬ ተዐውቀ is the chapter's closing formula, as at the end of ch. 77 ('So now it is known that the king of Persia is of the seed of Shem'): ናሁ 'behold' + -ኬ, then ተዐውቀ 'it has become known', the tä-stem of ዐወቀ, rendered as a present. ንጉሠ ሞአብሂ 'the king of Moab too' (construct + -ሂ). ከመ ዘርአ ሴም ውእቱ 'that he is of the seed of Shem'. The ፨ ፨ ፨ run closes the chapter and belongs to this unit.

sentences.t: ፸፱ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ዓማሌቅ ።
sentences.l: 79. Concerning king-of Amalek.
sentences.i: Chapter 79: Concerning the King of Amalek
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፸፱ is the Ethiopic numeral 70 + 9 = 79. በእንተ 'concerning' with the construct chain ንጉሠ ዓማሌቅ 'king-of Amalek'. Amalek is the people and its ancestor; the chapter derives the king from Ammon, the son of Lot's younger daughter.

sentences.t: ወሶበ ፡ ወለደት ፡ እንተ ፡ ትልህቅ ፡ ትቤላ ፡ ለእንተ ፡ ትንእስ ፡ ሀቢኬ ፡ ናስትዮ ፡ ወይነ ፡ ለአቡነ ፡ ወአንቲኒ ፡ ከመ ፡ ትባኢ ፡ ኀቤሁ ፡ እመ ፡ ትረክቢ ፡ ውሉደ ፡ ወካዕበ ፡ ገብራ ፡ ወይነ ፡ ወደገማ ፡ ቃለ ፡ እበድ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብላ ፡ ስተይ ፡ ወይነ ፡ ኦአቡነ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይትናዘዝ ፡ ልብከ ፤
sentences.l: And-when she-bore she who is-elder, she-said-to-her to-she who is-younger: come-now let-us-make-drink wine to-our-father, and-you-also that you-enter to-him, if you-find children; and-again they-made wine, and-they-repeated word-of fool, while they-say: drink wine, O our-father, that it-be-comforted your-heart;
sentences.i: When the elder had given birth, she said to the younger: 'Come, let us make our father drink wine, and you also, that you may go in to him if you can get children.' And again they prepared wine, and repeated a foolish speech, saying: 'Drink wine, our father, that your heart may be comforted.'
sentences.n: ወሶበ ወለደት እንተ ትልህቅ: the elder is the subject, 'she who is elder'. ትቤላ ለእንተ ትንእስ 'she said to her, to the younger' (ትቤላ is the feminine of the defective verb ይቤ with -ላ 'to her'). ሀቢኬ I read as ሀቢ ('give', the feminine imperative used as an exhortation, 'come now') + -ኬ (?). ናስትዮ is the 1cp subjunctive of the ʾa-stem of ሰትየ, with -ዮ 'him': 'let us make him drink'. ወአንቲኒ 'and you also'. ከመ ትባኢ ኀቤሁ 'that you enter to him' (ቦአ, the 2fs subjunctive); እመ ትረክቢ ውሉደ 'if you find children', ረከበ 'find, get'. ገብራ is here a 3fp perfect 'they made' (it was glossed as 'her servant' in an earlier part, but the sense here is the verb); ወደገማ 'and they repeated' (ደገመ 'repeat'). ቃለ እበድ 'word-of a fool' (a construct chain), meaning a foolish speech; I take እበድ as 'fool' (?). እንዘ ይብላ 'while they say' (3fp imperfect). ስተይ is the imperative 'drink'; ኦ is the vocative 'O'. ይትናዘዝ is the tä-stem 'be comforted'. This unit follows Genesis 19:34, where the elder proposes the same plan to the younger.

sentences.t: ወውእቱሰ ፡ የዋህ ፡ ሰትየ ፡ ወሰክረ ።
sentences.l: And-he-as-for simple he-drank and-he-was-drunk.
sentences.i: And he, being a guileless man, drank and became drunk.
sentences.n: ወውእቱሰ 'but he, as for him' (-ሰ contrastive). የዋህ 'guileless, simple' is the adjective in apposition. ሰትየ 'he drank' and ወሰክረ 'and he was drunk' (3ms perfects). This is a gentle word in the text's favour of Lot; the earlier unit called him ጻድቅ 'righteous'.

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ሰትየ ፡ ወጸልመ ፡ ልቡ ፡ ቦአት ፡ እንተ ፡ ትንእስ ፡ ወሰከበት ፡ ምስሌሁ ፡ ወውእቱሰ ፡ ካዕበ ፡ ኢያእመረ ፡ በሰኪቦታ ፡ ወበተንሥኦታ ።
sentences.l: And-again when he-drank and-it-darkened his-heart, she-entered she who is-younger and-she-lay with-him, and-he-as-for again not-he-knew in-her-lying-down and-in-her-rising.
sentences.i: And again, when he had drunk and his mind was clouded, the younger went in and lay with him, and again he did not know when she lay down or when she rose.
sentences.n: ወካዕበ 'and again' (ካዕበ 'again, a second time'). ሶበ ሰትየ ወጸልመ ልቡ 'when he drank and his heart was darkened', as in the last unit and the one for the elder. ቦአት 'she entered' (3fs perfect of ቦአ), with እንተ ትንእስ 'she who is younger' as subject. ወሰከበት ምስሌሁ 'and she lay with him'. ወውእቱሰ ካዕበ ኢያእመረ is the same wording as for the elder, with ካዕበ 'again'; በሰኪቦታ ወበተንሥኦታ 'at her lying down and her rising' (Genesis 19:35).

sentences.t: ወካዕበ ፡ ይእቲኒ ፡ ፀንሰት ፡ ወወለደት ፡ ወልደ ፡ ወሰመየቶ ፡ ስሞ ፡ ዓሞን ፤
sentences.l: And-again she-also she-conceived and-she-bore son, and-she-named-him his-name Ammon;
sentences.i: She too conceived and bore a son, and named him Ammon;
sentences.n: ወካዕበ ይእቲኒ 'and again she too' (ይእቲ 'she' + -ኒ). ፀንሰት ወወለደት 'she conceived and bore'; ወልደ 'a son' is the accusative object. ዓሞን is the Geʿez of Ammon, the Ammonites' ancestor in Genesis 19:38, where the child is named Ben-ammi 'son of my kin'. This text does not give the meaning; Genesis 19:38 does.

sentences.t: ወውእቱ ፡ ንጉሦሙ ፡ ለዓማሌቃውያን ፡ ወናሁኬ ፡ ተዐውቀ ፡ ከመ ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ዓማሌቅ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዘርአ ፡ ሤም ፡ ውእቱ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-he king-of-them to-Amalekites; and-behold-indeed it-became-known that king-of Amalek that seed-of Shem he. ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: He is the king of the Amalekites; and so now it is known that the king of Amalek is of the seed of Shem.
sentences.n: ወውእቱ ንጉሦሙ ለዓማሌቃውያን: 'and he is their king, of the Amalekites' (ንጉሥ + -ሙ 'their', then ለ- + the people's name naming the owners). Here the text treats the son of Lot's younger daughter as father of Amalek; Genesis makes Ammon father of the Ammonites and Amalek a descendant of Esau (Genesis 36:12), so this chapter's account is the text's own. ወናሁኬ ተዐውቀ repeats the closing formula of ch. 78 (and ch. 77); ሤም is a spelling of ሴም 'Shem'. The run of eight ፨ closes the chapter and belongs to this last unit.
